subject.title: Sub-agent startup silence: no first-progress signal, aborted runs appear as hangs

question: Should OpenClaw add a new sub-agent lifecycle event contract such as `first-progress` and `startup-failed`, or solve startup silence through existing lifecycle phases plus richer terminal metadata/diagnostics?
rationale: The useful fix is not just a local bug patch; it defines new core lifecycle semantics that cross agent runtime, gateway wait/session projection, SDK normalization, docs, and compatibility expectations.

options.title: Approve a refreshed lifecycle contract
options.body: Land a current-main implementation of explicit progress/startup-failure phases with consumer handling and compatibility proof across the active runtime surfaces.

options.title: Use existing phases with richer metadata
options.body: Avoid new phase strings and instead make start/end/error terminal metadata distinguish startup aborts, with diagnostics and tests proving parent waits unblock correctly.

options.title: Defer pending root-cause isolation
options.body: Keep the issue open but require a fresh live reproduction or narrower sandbox-startup root-cause proof before accepting a core event-surface change.

recommendation.title: Approve a refreshed lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Land a current-main implementation of explicit progress/startup-failure phases with consumer handling and compatibility proof across the active runtime surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent broad lifecycle edits put this person closest to the active cross-surface lifecycle code that would define the permanent contract.
